exchanges: Hi there. I need help planning something, but first can I vent about tennis for a second?
Of course, vent away.
My doubles partner Wei and I lost in the club semis today. 6-4, 6-4. We were so close.
Two close sets hurt. What decided it?
Mostly my serve. I double-faulted at 4-5 twice. Wei was really nice about it.
That's a good partner. Double faults under pressure happen to everyone.
He's a patient guy, which makes sense since he teaches piano to little kids all week.
Working with young kids would build patience like nothing else.
Anyway. The actual planning thing: my friend Chidi and I are walking the Portuguese Camino in September, starting from Porto.
That's a beautiful route. Are you doing the coastal path or the central one?
coastal I think. chidi wants the ocean views
The coastal route is lovely, though it can be windier. It joins the central route near Redondela.
how many days is it from porto to santiago roughly
Around ten to thirteen days for most walkers, depending on daily distance.
ok we have two weeks so that works. I'm a little worried about my nonna while I'm away though.
Is she unwell?
She has diabetes and has been forgetting her insulin. My mom checks on her, but still.
That's a real worry. Phone reminders set up by your mom might help while you're gone.
Good idea. Her sister, my great-aunt Carla, lives with her, but Carla has bad arthritis in her hands so she can't help with the injections.
That makes it harder. A pharmacist might be able to suggest an easier pen device.
I'll look into it. Ok back to the Camino. What shoes?
Trail runners are popular on the Portuguese route because much of it is paved or packed trail. Break them in well beforehand.
Elif at the club walked the French route last year and swore by hers.
Then ask her which model. Firsthand advice from someone who has done the distance is gold.
She's the club pro, she's got like four pairs of everything lol
Comes with the job, I suppose.
Chidi's brother Emeka might join us for the last few days.
That's nice, a bit of a reunion at the end.
Yeah, he's finally done with school. He just started at a brewery and has to ask for time off.
First-job time-off requests can be awkward, but a few days is reasonable.
Oh, I need to fix something. Wei doesn't teach piano, he teaches guitar. I was thinking of his wife, she's the piano one.
Got it, a musical household. That explains the patience either way.
Haha yes. Their house is very loud.
Loud in the best way, hopefully.
Do you think I need a credencial in advance?
You can get one in Porto at the cathedral, so there's no need to order it ahead, though some people do.
Ok, easier. Should we book albergues or just show up?
In September the coastal route can be busy, so booking a night or two ahead is wise, especially in smaller towns.
chidi is a planner so he'll love that
Then he can take charge of bookings.
He already has a spreadsheet, honestly.
Of course he does.
Back to tennis. I want to fix my serve before the next tournament.
A lesson focused only on the toss might help, since toss errors cause most double faults.
Yeah my toss drifts right. Elif said the same.
Then that's the thing to work on. Practising tosses without hitting can help.
The next tournament is in November, a mixed doubles one.
That's enough time to rebuild the serve.
I'm partnering with Ingrid for that, she's new to the club and plays left-handed.
A lefty in mixed doubles can be a real advantage, the spin comes from an unfamiliar side.
She also moved here from Bergen, so she's used to playing indoors all winter.
That's handy, since your club season will move indoors soon too.
Exactly. Ok I'm going to go stretch, my shoulder is sore.
Good idea, go easy on it.

questions.message: What health issue does my great-aunt have again?
Where did Chidi's brother get a job?
Wei's the piano guy, isn't he?
Where was Ingrid living before she came here?
Does Chidi have any health problems I should plan around?
My shoulder actually feels a bit better after some stretching.
